code: Raw input is copied into the memory BIO attached to the SSL client
note: The client consumes attacker-controlled TLS bytes.

code: SSL_do_handshake interprets the bytes as a TLS handshake transcript
note: Malformed handshake contents steer state transitions and error cleanup.

code: The client allocates peer_tmp and a DH object while parsing a DHE ServerKeyExchange
note: This is the key object that becomes owned by the connection state.

code: EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh) transfers ownership to the EVP_PKEY wrapper
note: After assignment, peer_tmp aliases the same DH heap object.

code: On later validation failure the err path frees both DH and peer_tmp
note: If the object was already attached elsewhere, the wrapper can become stale.

code: Connection cleanup frees s->s3.peer_tmp again when the SSL object is torn down
note: The same wrapper is released during teardown.

code: The wrapped DH object is decremented through CRYPTO_DOWN_REF during EVP_PKEY/DH cleanup
note: This is the memory-safety sink when the freed DH storage is touched again.
